html:
The growing of groundnuts (peanuts) for export, which spread in Senegal from the 1840s, when French oil mills began buying them, and became the base of the colonial economy.

Farmers in Cayor, Baol and Sine-Saloum, the groundnut basin, grew them to pay taxes and buy rice, and seasonal migrants came from Mali and Guinea to work the fields. The railways were built largely to move the crop to the ports. The Mouride brotherhood became the greatest organiser of groundnut farming. The crop wore out the soil and left the country exposed to world prices and drought. Groundnuts are still a main crop of Senegal and of the Gambia.
